title: Section 299 — Deliberate and malicious acts, intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by insulting its religion or religious beliefs

content.overview: BNS s. 299 — Deliberate and malicious acts, intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by insulting its religion or religious beliefs.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Deliberate and malicious acts, intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by insulting its religion or religious beliefs. BNS restatement of IPC 295A. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 295A. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 299 is the rule on “Deliberate and malicious acts, intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by insulting its religion or religious beliefs”. The section provides that . Whoever, with deliberate and malicious intention of outraging the religious feelings of any class of citizens of India, by words, either spoken or written, or by signs or by visible representations or through electronic means or otherwise, insults or attempts to insult the religion or the religious beliefs of that class, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 299 exists so that “Deliberate and malicious acts, intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by insulting its religion or religious beliefs” has a closed legal test in Chapter XVI — Of Offences Relating to Religion. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.

Statutory Title: Deliberate and malicious acts, intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by insulting its religion or religious beliefs.

Core Legal Mandate: . Whoever, with deliberate and malicious intention of outraging the religious feelings of any class of citizens of India, by words, either spoken or written, or by signs or by visible representations ...
Classification and Sentencing: Structured under Chapter XVI penal tiers.
Evidentiary and Procedural Cognate: Governed by the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
essentialIngredients: The commission of an act or omission falling within the statutory description of Deliberate and malicious acts, intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by insulting its religion or religious beliefs.
The existence of the requisite culpable mental state (intention, knowledge, rashness, or negligence) prescribed under Section 299.
The absence of any statutory justification, exception, or lawful authority under Chapter III (General Exceptions).
The resulting consequence or endangerment specified in the statutory formula of Section 299.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 299 carries forward IPC 295A. It penalizes whoever, with deliberate and malicious intention of outraging the religious feelings of any class of citizens of India, by words, signs, or visible representations, insults or attempts to insult the religion or religious beliefs of that class, with imprisonment up to three years, fine, or both. The Supreme Court in Ramji Lal Modi held that the section does not penalize every casual or careless insult; liability strictly requires proof of 'deliberate and malicious' intent.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of deliberate and malicious acts, intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by insulting its religion or religious beliefs under Section 299 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 299.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 299 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 299 vs Section 302: Section 299 requires deliberate and malicious intent to outrage feelings (up to 3 years); Section 302 covers uttering words with deliberate intent to wound feelings (up to 1 year).
Section 299 vs Section 194 (Hate speech): Section 299 protects religious beliefs from malicious insult; Section 194 focuses on promoting enmity between different groups.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 299 for conduct relating to deliberate and malicious acts, intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by insulting its religion or religious beliefs.
Rule: Under BNS s. 299, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 299.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 299 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
